text:
maria: seeing a spike of ALB target deregistrations in us-west-2 during the GPU pool scale-up this morning. around ~10 pods dropped in ~5m, all SHOWING Unhealthy on ALB. :frowning_face:

sam: yup got alerted. healthchecks are timing out 10s. ALB logs show TCP resets from the targets. suspect egress/NAT pressure.

maria: logs from the pods show model shard downloads at startup, a ton of outbound connections to s3/edge-cdn. could that starve ephemeral ports?

alex: that's my first guess. when we spin GPUs up we pull multiple large artifacts concurrently. NAT gateway on that subnet has limited ephemeral ports per ENI -> SNAT exhaustion. ALB healthcheck packets might be getting dropped or reset when conntrack table is full.

sam: i pulled some metrics: conntrack count jumped from 40k -> 95k during the scale event, conntrack max is 100k on workers. also NAT gateway NAT64/port usage shows high port utilization.

jin: did we just push the kube-proxy/iptables change last night? might have changed ephemeral port allocation behavior.

maria: here's a clipped debug dump from one node during the event:
```
# ss -s
TCP:   52395 (estab 120, closed 51200, orphaned 0, timewait 5000)
Transport Total

# sudo conntrack -S | grep entries
total: 98782
```

sam: exact symptoms: ALB healthcheck intervals are normal but the target's TCP handshake never completes. client (ALB) sends SYN, we don't reply because SNAT/conntrack mapping exhausted and kernel drops new outbound mapping attempts.

alex: workaround options: 1) throttle model downloads (initContainer with concurrency control), 2) use S3 VPC endpoint so downloads don't consume NAT, 3) add NAT IP addresses / scale NAT pool, 4) move healthchecks to target group by IP vs instance? (not ideal).

maria: ops-bot reported some automated scale events too during the window. ops-bot, can you paste the autoscaler logs?

ops-bot: Autoscaler: started scale-up +5 nodes at 2026-03-18T10:12:31Z, finished at 10:14:05Z. Noted 3 consecutive node init failures (OOM on init container) and retried.

sam: init failures mean more restarts -> more repeated downloads -> worse egress pressure. vicious cycle.

jin: let's also check ip-masq config. if pods in that subnet are not using VPC CIDR in non-masq list they'll SNAT unnecessarily.

maria: good call. current ip-masq config: non-masquerade-cidr: 10.0.0.0/8 only. our artifact CDN IPs are public, so they SNAT through NAT.

alex: quick mitigation we can do in order: 1) patch GPU pool to use a startup hook that serializes artifact downloads (reduce parallelism to 2), 2) spin up an extra NAT gateway or add EIPs to existing NAT to increase port pool, 3) enable S3 gateway endpoint for the VPC, 4) lower kubelet pod eviction backoff to avoid repeated restarts.

maria: i'll open a short runbook ticket with these steps and apply the initContainer throttle first. would like a config change for S3 endpoint as medium-term.

sam: also adding an alert rule: if conntrack > 80% and ALB unhealthy targets > 1 -> page pager on-call. right now it was only paging infra slack.

jin: note for postmortem: check kernel upgrade PR from last night that changed nf_conntrack default limits. might need sysctl bump: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max from 100k -> 300k for those worker types.

alex: i can handle adding the S3 endpoint request + NAT IP bump. maria can you do initContainer change?

maria: on it. applying a quick rollout to the gpu-autoscale daemonset with a serialized-download script. will monitor ALB health. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-033, assigned to eng-infra. Initial impact: ALB target deregistrations during GPU pool scale-up causing transient 502/504s for edge inference traffic.

sam: thanks. once we have mitigations live, let's run a controlled scale-up to validate (stage first).
